items.title: Delhi court denies bail to lawyer accused in Satya Niketan building collapse
items.summary: A Delhi court on Monday denied bail to Shubham Tyagi, an advocate and one of the accused in the case related to the collapse of a paying-guest (PG) building in Satya Niketan that killed seven people. Additional Sessions Judge (ASJ) Dhirendra Rana of the Patiala House Courts said Tyagi, who was one of the operators of the PG, had failed to ensure the safety of students staying at the premises despite being aware of ongoing construction work in the building. The court noted that students had complained about the construction work, following which Tyagi and his co-accused Sudhanshu Lovenish Kumar allegedly threatened that they would have to vacate the premises if they continued raising objections. "He could have easily foreseen the danger on account of illegal construction activities but he prioritized his financial benefits above the life and safety of innocent students/labours," the Court said. It said that Tyagi is a lawyer and yet, he did not follow the law. Such accused persons must be dealt with an "iron hand", the Court added. "The court cannot turn blind eyes towards the fact that seven valuable lives have been lost and the impact of their death would be everlasting on their families," it underscored. Delhi court denies anticipatory bail to lawyer accused in Satya Niketan building collapse The building at Satya Niketan Market, which was being run as a hostel under the name "Hostel Daze," collapsed on September 6, killing five students and two labourers. Tyagi, who is enrolled with the Bar Council of Delhi (BCD), claimed he was merely a tenant and had no authority to undertake structural alterations. He also pointed out that the investigation was complete and the chargesheet had been filed. However, the Court refuted the arguments and rejected his bail application. Advocates Hemant Shah, Neeraj Kanwar, Vishal Mann, Ankita Gautam and Mayank Rana appeared for accused Shubham Tyagi. State was represented by additional public prosecutor Sanjay Jindal. [Read Order]
